title: Coherent finite scalar restriction for sheafified and derived open extension
statement:
For finite commutative rings $A,B,C$ and homomorphisms $\varphi:A\to B$, $\psi:B\to C$, put $\chi=\psi\varphi$. For each scheme $T$ use constant ring sheaves on its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Write $r_{\varphi,T}$ for restriction of module-sheaf scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] and for its exact termwise functor on the unbounded derived categories. Write $\rho_T:r_{\varphi,T}r_{\psi,T}\xrightarrow{\sim}r_{\chi,T}$ for the canonical identification: on underlying abelian sheaves it is the identity and the two actions are $a m=\psi_T(\varphi_T(a))m$; on derived categories it is its termwise localization [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization].

Let $j:U\hookrightarrow Z$ be an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. For $R=A,B,C$, let $J_R=j_!^R$ be sheafified extension by zero [def-weil-extension-by-zero], which is exact [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-exact]; $J_R$ also denotes its termwise localization. There is a natural isomorphism of module-sheaf functors
$$e_\varphi:J_A r_{\varphi,U}\xrightarrow{\sim}r_{\varphi,Z}J_B,$$
uniquely characterized by inducing the identity on the defining extension-by-zero presheaves before sheafification. It induces a natural isomorphism with the same endpoints on all of $D(U_{\mathrm{proet}},B)$. For every $C$-module sheaf, every complex thereof and every $K\in D(U_{\mathrm{proet}},C)$, respectively, these specified comparisons satisfy
$$e_{\chi,K}\circ J_A(\rho_{U,K})=\rho_{Z,J_CK}\circ r_{\varphi,Z}(e_{\psi,K})\circ e_{\varphi,r_{\psi,U}K}.$$
For an identity coefficient map the comparison is the identity under the canonical identifications. No quasi-compactness of $j$, flatness of coefficient maps, boundedness or constructibility assumption is imposed.

source.place: Tag 03DI, label lemma-extension-by-zero: sheafified extension-by-zero construction; coefficient coherence and its unbounded localization are the agent-written argument extracted from former steps 2–3 of lem-sf-compact-support-restriction-of-scalars.

proof.text: For a $B_U$-module sheaf $M$, write $P_M$ for the defining extension presheaf. The formula in [def-weil-extension-by-zero] gives a canonical identity $P_{r_{\varphi,U}M}=r_{\varphi,Z}P_M$ of $A_Z$-module presheaves: if $V\to Z$ factors through $U$, both values are the abelian group $M(V\to U)$ with action $a m=\varphi_Z(a)m$; otherwise both are zero. The restriction maps and maps induced by morphisms of $M$ are identical, since scalar restriction changes only the action. For two coefficient maps the sectionwise identity also identifies both successive actions with $a m=\psi_Z(\varphi_Z(a))m$; it is precisely the prescribed $\rho$, on both sheaves and presheaves.

source.place: Tag 03DI, label lemma-extension-by-zero, and Tag 03CY, label lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules; agent-written coefficient comparison using their explicit construction and universal property

proof.text: Let $aP$ denote abelian sheafification and $\eta_P:P\to aP$ its unit. By [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], both $J_A r_{\varphi,U}M$ and $r_{\varphi,Z}J_BM$ have underlying abelian sheaf $aP_M$, canonically identified by the identity on the presheaves of step 1. On the second object the restricted $A_Z$-action extends the action on $r_{\varphi,Z}P_M$, because $\eta_{P_M}$ is $B_Z$-linear and hence $A_Z$-linear. Uniqueness of the extended action makes this exactly the action on the first object. The canonical underlying identity and its inverse are therefore $A_Z$-linear and define $e_{\varphi,M}$. It satisfies $e_{\varphi,M}\circ\eta_{P_{r_\varphi M}}=r_{\varphi,Z}(\eta_{P_M})$, using step 1's identification. The unique factorization clause of the cited sheafification statement shows that this equation determines $e_{\varphi,M}$ uniquely.

source.place: Tag 03DI, label lemma-extension-by-zero, and Tag 03CY, label lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules; agent-written coefficient comparison using their explicit construction and universal property

proof.text: For a $B_U$-linear map $f:M\to N$, precompose $r_{\varphi,Z}(J_B f)\circ e_{\varphi,M}$ and $e_{\varphi,N}\circ J_A(r_{\varphi,U}f)$ with $\eta_{P_{r_\varphi M}}$. By the unit equation of step 2 and functoriality of sheafification, both become $r_{\varphi,Z}(\eta_{P_N}\circ P_f)$. The unique factorization clause therefore proves naturality. For $\varphi=\mathrm{id}$ the identity on $J_AM$ satisfies the same unit equation, so uniqueness gives the identity comparison under the canonical identifications.

source.place: Tag 03DI, label lemma-extension-by-zero, and Tag 03CY, label lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules; agent-written coefficient comparison using their explicit construction and universal property

proof.text: Fix a $C_U$-module sheaf $M$. Both sides of the required cocycle are $A_Z$-linear maps from $J_A r_{\varphi,U}r_{\psi,U}M$ to $r_{\chi,Z}J_CM$. Precompose with $\eta_{P_{r_\varphi r_\psi M}}$ and use step 1's identities. On the left, naturality of the sheafification unit for $P(\rho_{U,M})$, followed by the unit equation for $e_\chi$, gives $r_{\chi,Z}(\eta_{P_M})$. On the right, the unit equations for $e_\varphi$ and $e_\psi$ give $r_{\varphi,Z}r_{\psi,Z}(\eta_{P_M})$, followed by $\rho_{Z,J_CM}$. Since $\rho$ is the identity on underlying presheaves, this is the same map $r_{\chi,Z}(\eta_{P_M})$. Unique factorization through sheafification proves exactly the displayed equation, including both specified $\rho$ components.

source.place: Tag 03DI, label lemma-extension-by-zero, and Tag 03CY, label lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules; agent-written coefficient comparison using their explicit construction and universal property

proof.text: Scalar restriction is additive by [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] and preserves finite limits and finite colimits by [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-coefficient-ordinary-adjunction], applied on each small pro-etale site to its constant-ring sheaf map; thus it is exact. Each $J_R$ is exact by [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-exact]. Consequently [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] applies to all these functors on unbounded cochain complexes and derived categories. Apply the sheaf comparison in each degree to a complex: its commutation with the differential is naturality from step 3. Its inverse likewise is a chain map. The cocycle and identity laws for complexes hold degree by degree by step 4 and the identity law of step 3.

source.place: Tag 015F, label lemma-right-derived-exact-functor, with sites-modules.tex Tag 03DA (lemma-abelian) and the cited ordinary scalar-restriction exactness statement

proof.text: Let $Q_R$ be the localization from complexes of $R$-module sheaves to $D(U_{\mathrm{proet}},R)$, and use the exact factorizations of step 5. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] descends the chain isomorphism to $e_\varphi:J_A r_{\varphi,U}\cong r_{\varphi,Z}J_B$ on all of $D(U_{\mathrm{proet}},B)$. Descend $\rho$ by the same rule. Under the factorization isomorphisms, precomposition with $Q_C$ identifies each factor of the desired derived cocycle with its chain-level factor: for a whiskered transformation this follows from its component formula at a complex, and clause (2)'s uniqueness identifies its lift. Composition and identity are preserved by clause (2). The two resulting natural transformations agree after precomposition with $Q_C$ by step 5, hence agree on the whole derived category by clause (3). The same argument gives the identity coefficient law. Neither this localization theorem nor the exact factorization restricts the degrees of a complex. The presheaf and sheafification arguments never required quasi-compactness, flatness or constructibility.
